report:
Fresh review of the complete checking_scope claim and all six ordinary implementation entries and eleven associated ordinary tests. No TODO/N/A entry is attached. Scope here is harness demand/traversal and explicit unsupported-work handling, not independently judging authored expression dereference semantics. I read current captured source and test assertions and captured additional preparation, body-interface and module-completeness dependencies. No source changes, new tests, Cargo build or test execution in this review; central passing suites are not the basis of this source assessment.

Demand policy: observe.rs collect invokes check_crate(db, root) before forming observation targets. check_crate takes only the local root, not markers, visibility or entry points. walk_module checks unexpanded error items and expansion completeness and iterates expanded module symbols; local modules recurse. walk_symbol requests each local function signature and invokes body for each present body, including private functions, then retains body diagnostics. Struct signatures/fields and enum, trait and impl signatures are explicitly demanded; trait/impl associated items recurse through the same dispatcher. External symbol variants are deliberately no-ops, so importing/using external signatures does not schedule eager dependency-body traversal. Marker processing selects output after these demands. The captured prepare path does not condition collect on observations, and combines independent rustc and Sage results so a rustc error cannot be mistaken for successful Sage validation.

Other implementation entries: local_syms/associated.rs enumerates the owner's source associated CST and lowers every supported function/type/const into an owner-scoped local symbol; the harness dispatches each, rather than demanding only referenced methods. parse/items.rs retains enum discriminants as expression pointers and rejects unsupported associated-body syntax before enumerating supported members. parse/mod.rs turns malformed or unsupported enabled items into explicit Error entries, including dangling attributes, instead of dropping them. local_syms/uses.rs supplies an explicit import-resolution diagnostic pass even for unused imports; walk_symbol demands it. cst/enums.rs stores discriminants and emits their source span when rendering tokens, preserving their presence across source transformations. These six entries together support traversal through source/expanded members and visible failure for unsupported work. The captured module-completeness helper applies the symbol-listing policy, checks unexpanded errors/active attributes, macro completeness, children and derive completeness; the harness emits an explicit incomplete-expansion diagnostic when it fails.

Unsupported work is not represented as implemented: const/static/type-alias items and residual macro invocations get a whole-crate unsupported diagnostic. Associated unsupported items get an explicit diagnostic/error item. Enum discriminants get their own unsupported diagnostic at the retained expression span; this claim expressly permits that alternative to checking. Malformed bodies/items remain failures through parser error entries. No future narrower entry-point mode is exposed by this policy.

All eleven tests: (1) unselected_private_body_still_reports_errors requires the same Sage mismatch for an erroneous private body with no marker and with a ty marker added to a different function, directly testing selector independence. (2) macro_generated_errors_match_the_invocation expects the generated function's mismatch at the invocation, proving expanded bodies are visited. (3) modules_and_associated_bodies supplies a real nested module file with a private impl method and asserts its completed u16 observation. (4) real_std checks a local signature using std::string::String with empty diagnostics, providing an external metadata integration scenario; the absence of eager external-body traversal is established primarily by the exhaustive external-symbol dispatch. (5) signature_diagnostics_are_retained_once expects one unresolved signature type despite two callers. (6) unused_import_is_checked expects an unresolved-import diagnostic without any use site. (7) enum_discriminant_body_is_not_silently_accepted accounts for rustc's error separately and requires both Sage mismatch and the explicit unsupported-discriminant message. (8) enum_discriminants_survive_syntax_token_rendering asserts two retained discriminants and exact token rendering including their expressions. (9) malformed_body_is_not_silently_accepted requires a Sage diagnostic mismatch for malformed private body syntax. (10) malformed_private_enum_signature_is_checked requires Sage's unresolved-type message for an unreferenced private enum. (11) valid_enum_discriminant_reports_sage_limitation expects only Sage's explicit unsupported diagnostic for rustc-valid syntax, so rustc cannot mask an omitted Sage check. Together the cases test traversal, signatures, private visibility, associated/submodule/expanded paths, marker independence and explicit unsupported behavior. Not every unsupported dispatcher arm has a distinct fixture, but they share the visible diagnostic helper; no silent-success branch or necessary edit was found in this demand-policy review.
